explanation.en: `int[] x = [90, 75, 88];` is a C# 12 collection expression; Java and Kotlin cannot initialise an array with square brackets, and `Console.WriteLine` with `$"..."` interpolation is C#.
`string?` nullable reference types, the `is not null` pattern and the implicit `args` of top-level statements are C#.
A `"""` raw string literal assigned with `var` and closed by `;`, then printed with `Console.WriteLine`, is C# 11. Python has triple quotes but no `var` or semicolons.
An index initialiser `["Ada"] = 36` inside `new Dictionary<string, int> { ... }` and deconstructing each pair with `foreach (var (name, age) in ...)` are C#.
`public class Greeter(string greeting)` is a C# 12 primary constructor: the parameter has its type first and no `val`/`var`, unlike Kotlin, and top-level statements sit above the class.
The `required` modifier together with `{ get; init; }` accessors is C# 11; the compiler forces callers to set `Host` in the object initializer.
`static async Task<int>` with `await Task.Delay` is the C# Task-based async model; top-level statements allow a local function and `await` with no `Main`.
A file-scoped `namespace X;` plus `[ApiController]`, `[Route]` and `[HttpGet("{id:int}")]` attributes on a `ControllerBase` subclass is an ASP.NET Core controller in C#.
`??=` assigns only when the left side is null and `?.` skips the call on null; with `string?` and `Console.WriteLine` this is C# (Kotlin has `?.` but no `??=`).

codeSnippet:
var rows = from o in orders
           join c in customers on o.CustomerId equals c.Id
           orderby o.Total descending
           select new { c.Name, o.Total };

explanation.en: LINQ query syntax with `join ... on ... equals ...`, `orderby ... descending` and an anonymous type `new { c.Name, o.Total }` is C#; no other mainstream language has `equals` as a join keyword.
`data is [var first, .., var last]` is a C# 11 list pattern: `..` is a slice pattern matching any middle elements.
`where T : INumber<T>` and `T.Zero` use C# 11 generic math (static abstract interface members from System.Numerics); `Sum<double>([1.5, 2.5])` passes a collection expression.
